title: PTE Australia
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public PTE syllabus. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: A report explains that remote work lowers commuting emissions but raises household electricity use, so the net effect depends on how each home is heated. What is the writer's overall conclusion about remote work and emissions?
options: Its overall effect depends on how homes are heated.
It has no effect on emissions at all.
items.explanation: The passage credits remote work with cutting commuting emissions yet notes that home energy use rises, so the net result turns on how each home is heated.

items.stem: A notice states that candidates may book the computer-delivered test up to three times within a twelve-month period. According to the notice, how many times may a candidate book the test in twelve months?
items.explanation: The notice states plainly that the test may be booked up to three times within a twelve-month period, so the other figures are not supported.

items.stem: A text notes that the evidence for the new method is tentative and must be confirmed by larger trials. In the passage, the word tentative most nearly means which of the following?
items.explanation: Because the evidence still needs confirmation by larger trials, tentative means provisional or not yet certain rather than proven or false.

items.stem: A study finds that students who reviewed their notes within a day recalled more than those who waited a week, though the sample was small. What can reasonably be inferred?
options: Early review has no effect on recall.
The study proves review is useless.
Waiting a week always improves recall.
Early review may aid recall, but the finding needs a larger sample.
items.explanation: The early reviewers recalled more, which points to a benefit, but the small sample means the result is suggestive rather than conclusive.

items.stem: A passage describes how urban trees cool streets, absorb pollution and reduce flooding, while noting that they also need water and maintenance. What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Urban trees bring several benefits but also require care.
Urban trees are too costly to plant.
Urban trees have no measurable benefits.
Urban trees should be removed from cities.
items.explanation: The passage lists cooling, pollution absorption and flood reduction as benefits and adds a maintenance caveat, so the main idea balances benefits with care.

items.stem: An article outlines the arguments for and against a four-day working week and ends by calling for more controlled trials. What is the author's main purpose?
options: To present both sides and urge further testing
To prove that one side is dishonest
items.explanation: The article sets out opposing arguments and closes by requesting more controlled trials, so its purpose is balanced presentation followed by a call for evidence.

items.stem: Four sentences must be reordered into a paragraph. Three describe the causes of coastal erosion, while one introduces the topic by defining coastal erosion. Which sentence should come first?
options: A sentence about the causes of erosion
A sentence giving a specific example
The sentence that defines coastal erosion
A sentence offering a possible solution
items.explanation: A paragraph normally opens with a topic sentence that defines or introduces the subject, so the definition of coastal erosion should come first.

items.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence. The committee could not reach a decision because the members held views that were fundamentally what with one another?
items.explanation: A committee that cannot decide is divided, so views that are fundamentally incompatible fit best, while identical or adjacent views would point to agreement.

items.stem: In the sentence 'The council funded the new library because it served a growing suburb,' what does the word it refer to?
items.explanation: The pronoun it refers to the thing that serves the suburb, which is the new library, rather than the council, the suburb or the funding.

items.stem: A profile of the exam lists listening, reading, speaking and writing as the assessed areas. Which area is NOT listed among the assessed areas?
items.explanation: The profile names listening, reading, speaking and writing, so numerical reasoning is the one area that is not listed among the assessed skills.

items.stem: A reviewer calls the new policy a bold experiment but warns that it may create as many problems as it solves. What is the reviewer's attitude toward the policy?
items.explanation: Calling the policy bold acknowledges its ambition while the warning about new problems adds doubt, which together signal a cautiously critical attitude.

items.stem: A passage explains that coral bleaching happens when warm water makes corals expel the algae that feed them, which turns the reef white. Which summary best matches the passage?
options: Corals turn white in order to attract more fish.
Cold water causes reefs to flourish.
Algae make the surrounding water warmer.
Warm water causes corals to lose the algae that feed them, bleaching the reef.
items.explanation: The passage links bleaching to warm water that drives corals to expel their algae, so the summary about losing the feeding algae matches the text.

items.stem: An essay argues that testing on animals is unreliable because the results often fail to predict human responses, and it adds that ethical objections reinforce this view. Which point supports the author's argument?
options: Animal results often fail to predict human responses.
items.explanation: The statement that animal results often fail to predict human responses is the evidence the author uses to argue that animal testing is unreliable.

items.stem: A text reports that when a city introduced congestion charging, traffic fell and bus journeys became faster. What was one reported effect of the charge?
items.explanation: The text reports two effects of the charge, a fall in traffic and faster bus journeys, so faster bus journeys is the option supported by the passage.

items.stem: A passage contrasts two energy sources, noting that solar panels are cheap to run but produce nothing at night, while gas plants run at any hour but emit carbon. Which statement reflects the contrast?
options: Both sources run only at night.
Gas is cheaper to run than solar.
Solar is cheap but intermittent, while gas runs continuously but emits carbon.
Solar emits more carbon than gas.
items.explanation: The passage sets solar's low running cost and night-time gap against gas's continuous output and carbon emissions, which is exactly this contrast.

items.stem: A recipe for compost explains that you collect scraps, layer them with dry leaves, turn the pile weekly, and wait until it darkens. What happens immediately after collecting the scraps?
items.explanation: The steps are given in order, so layering the scraps with dry leaves comes directly after collecting them, with turning and waiting later on.

items.stem: A text says the two findings are correlated, meaning they tend to change together, though neither necessarily causes the other. In the passage, correlated means what?
items.explanation: The text defines correlation as a tendency to change together while denying that one necessarily causes the other, so the first option matches the definition.

items.stem: A survey reports that of 500 commuters, 60 per cent drive and the rest use public transport. How many of the commuters use public transport?
items.explanation: Sixty per cent of 500 is 300 drivers, and the remaining 40 per cent, which is 200 commuters, use public transport.

items.stem: A table shows pass rates rising each year from 2019 to 2022 and then falling in 2023. What does the table show about the pass rates over this period?
options: Steady growth followed by a decline
items.explanation: The rates climb every year through 2022 and then drop in 2023, which is steady growth followed by a decline.

items.stem: A paragraph describes the water cycle. One sentence introduces evaporation, while others explain condensation, precipitation and collection. Which sentence should open the paragraph?
options: A concluding sentence about water use
items.explanation: The paragraph should open with the sentence that introduces the first stage, evaporation, before condensation, precipitation and collection follow in sequence.

items.stem: In a lecture a speaker says online learning saves travel time but can leave students feeling isolated, so institutions should build in peer contact. What does the speaker recommend?
options: Building peer contact into online courses
items.explanation: The speaker notes isolation as a drawback and responds by advising institutions to build in peer contact, which is the recommendation given.

items.stem: A campus announcement says the library closes at 8 pm on weekdays but stays open until midnight during exam weeks. When does the library close during exam weeks?
items.explanation: The announcement extends the weekday closing time to midnight during exam weeks, so midnight is when the library closes in that period.

items.stem: In a talk the speaker states that the experiment was repeated to check whether the results were what. Which word best completes the speaker's sentence?
items.explanation: Repeating an experiment is done to confirm that its results are trustworthy, so reliable is the word that completes the sentence naturally.

items.stem: A speaker says the new timetable is an improvement on balance, though the morning buses remain unreliable. What is the speaker's attitude toward the timetable?
options: Broadly positive but critical of the morning buses
items.explanation: Calling the timetable an improvement is positive, while the complaint about unreliable morning buses makes the attitude broadly positive yet critical.

items.stem: A student says, 'I am sorry to interrupt, but could I ask one quick question about the deadline.' Why does the student speak this way?
options: To interrupt politely and ask about the deadline
items.explanation: The apologetic opening followed by a request for one quick question shows the student is interrupting politely to ask about the deadline.

items.stem: A podcast explains that bees pollinate many crops, but that pesticide use and disease are reducing their numbers, which threatens food supplies. Which summary is most accurate?
options: Bees harm crops and are increasing in number.
Bees pollinate crops but are declining because of pesticides and disease, which threatens food supplies.
Pesticides help bees to pollinate more crops.
Food supplies are unaffected by changes in bee numbers.
items.explanation: The podcast credits bees with pollinating crops, blames pesticides and disease for their decline, and links that decline to a threat to food supplies.

items.stem: A manager tells a colleague that the report must be ready by Thursday at the latest because the board meets on Friday. Why must the report be ready by Thursday?
options: Because the manager is on leave
Because Thursday is a public holiday
Because the board meets on Friday
items.explanation: The manager gives the reason directly, that the board meets on Friday, so the report is needed by Thursday for that meeting.

items.stem: A tour guide says the museum's Egyptian gallery is on the first floor, next to the cafe. Where is the Egyptian gallery?
options: On the first floor next to the cafe
items.explanation: The guide locates the Egyptian gallery on the first floor beside the cafe, so that is the position given in the recording.

items.stem: A speaker notes that although the bridge was completed on schedule, the budget overran by twenty per cent. What does this suggest about the project?
options: It finished on time but cost more than planned
It finished late and under budget
items.explanation: Completed on schedule means it finished on time, and a twenty per cent budget overrun means it cost more than planned, so the first option fits.

items.stem: In a recording the speaker says the team had to what the plan after the supplier withdrew. Which word best completes the sentence?
items.explanation: When a supplier withdraws a team must change its arrangements, so revise is the word that completes the sentence meaningfully.

items.stem: A lecturer explains that because the sample was drawn from one city, the findings may not apply to other regions. What limitation does the lecturer identify?
options: The sample came from only one city
items.explanation: The lecturer ties the limited applicability to a sample drawn from a single city, which is the limitation being identified.

items.stem: A caller says, 'I am calling about the invoice you sent, because the amount does not match our order.' What is the caller's purpose?
options: To query a discrepancy in an invoice
items.explanation: The caller points out that the invoice amount does not match the order, so the purpose is to query a discrepancy rather than to praise or order.

items.stem: A safety briefing states that staff must wear helmets in the loading bay but not in the office. Where must staff wear helmets?
items.explanation: The briefing names the loading bay as the place where helmets are required, and it explicitly excludes the office from that rule.

items.stem: A reviewer says the film starts slowly but rewards patient viewers with a powerful ending. What is the reviewer's view of the film?
options: A slow start is worth it for the strong ending
The film has no proper ending
items.explanation: The reviewer admits the slow start yet praises the rewarding, powerful ending, so the overall view is that the slow start is worthwhile.

items.stem: A talk explains that sleep helps the brain consolidate memories, so students who sleep well after studying tend to remember more. Which summary fits best?
options: Sleep has no effect on memory.
Studying is unnecessary if a person sleeps well.
Sleep helps the brain consolidate memories, which improves recall after study.
items.explanation: The talk links good sleep after study to better recall through memory consolidation, which is exactly what the first summary states.

items.stem: A speaker says the survey response rate was low, so the results should be treated with caution. What does the speaker advise?
items.explanation: The low response rate leads the speaker to advise caution in interpreting the results, rather than ignoring or fully trusting them.

items.stem: An announcement says the conference keynote begins at 9 am in Hall A, while the workshops begin at 11 am in Hall B. Where does the keynote take place?
items.explanation: The announcement places the keynote in Hall A, while Hall B is the venue for the workshops that begin later in the morning.

items.stem: In a recording the speaker says the two theories are not mutually what, since both can be true at once. Which word best completes the sentence?
items.explanation: Two ideas that can both be true at once are not mutually exclusive, so exclusive is the word that completes the sentence.

items.stem: A speaker describes a study in which participants who exercised daily reported a better mood than those who did not. What did the study compare?
items.explanation: The study contrasts participants who exercised daily with those who did not, so the comparison is between exercisers and non-exercisers.

items.stem: A guide warns that the path becomes slippery after rain and advises walkers to wear sturdy footwear. What does the guide imply?
options: The path is closed whenever it rains
Rain makes the path safer to use
Footwear does not matter on the path
Walkers should wear suitable shoes in wet conditions
items.explanation: Warning of a slippery path after rain and recommending sturdy footwear together imply that suitable shoes are needed in wet conditions.

items.stem: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence. The list of recommendations what been submitted to the committee.
items.explanation: The subject is the singular noun list, not the plural recommendations, so the singular verb has is required to agree with it.

items.stem: Choose the correct verb form. By the time the results were published, the team what on the project for three years.
items.explanation: The action continued up to a point in the past and lasted three years, so the past perfect continuous had been working is the correct form.

items.stem: Choose the correct preposition. The report focuses what the causes of urban flooding rather than its effects.
items.explanation: The verb focus is followed by the preposition on, so the report focuses on the causes of urban flooding.

items.stem: Choose the correct choice. She was appointed what head of the department after a competitive search.
items.explanation: Titles such as head of the department take no article when used after the verb appoint, so no article is needed here.

items.stem: Choose the correct form. If the council what the proposal, construction would begin next spring.
items.explanation: The main clause uses would begin, which forms a second conditional with the past simple approved in the if clause.

items.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to the underlined word. The committee reached a unanimous decision.
items.explanation: Unanimous means that everyone agreed, so a unanimous decision is one agreed by all rather than divided or postponed.

items.stem: Choose the correct word form. The findings were what enough to justify a larger trial.
items.explanation: The verb were needs a predicative adjective, and the adjective promising fits before the word enough to describe the findings.

items.stem: Choose the correct verb form. The museum what more than a million visitors since it reopened.
items.explanation: The word since points to a period continuing to the present, so the present perfect has attracted is the correct form.

items.stem: Choose the correct preposition. The two studies differ what their methods but agree on the main result.
items.explanation: The verb differ is followed by in when naming the area of difference, so the studies differ in their methods.

items.stem: Choose the correct linking word. The treatment was effective; what, it caused mild side effects in some patients.
items.explanation: The second clause contrasts a drawback with the benefit, so the contrastive linker however is correct rather than therefore or furthermore.

items.stem: Choose the word that best collocates. The government must what measures to reduce air pollution.
items.explanation: In English the standard collocation is take measures, so take is the verb that fits the sentence naturally.

items.stem: Choose the correct word form. The evidence was too what to support such a strong claim.
items.explanation: The adjective weak is needed after too to describe the evidence, whereas weakly, weaken and weakness are other word classes.

items.stem: Choose the correct form. Of the two proposals, the second is by far the what practical.
items.explanation: When comparing exactly two things, the comparative more is used, so the second proposal is the more practical of the two.

items.stem: Choose the correct word. The researchers published what findings in a leading journal.
items.explanation: The possessive determiner referring back to the plural researchers is their, while its, there and they are are the wrong forms.

items.stem: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to the underlined word. Food was abundant during the harvest.
items.explanation: Abundant means existing in large quantities, so its opposite is scarce, while plentiful, ample and sufficient are all near synonyms.

items.stem: Choose the correct form. The samples what to the laboratory before the results were analysed.
items.explanation: The samples received the action earlier than another past event, so the past perfect passive had been sent is the correct form.

items.stem: Choose the correct word. The new policy had a significant impact what small businesses.
items.explanation: The noun impact is followed by the preposition on when naming what is affected, so the policy had an impact on small businesses.

items.stem: Choose the word that best fits. The witness gave a what account of the events, describing them in careful detail.
items.explanation: Describing events in careful detail signals a detailed account, whereas vague, reluctant and silent all contradict the clue.

items.stem: Choose the correct modal. Passengers what fasten their seatbelts before take-off because it is a legal requirement.
items.explanation: A legal requirement expresses obligation, so the modal must is correct, while might, could and would express possibility rather than obligation.

items.stem: Choose the correct word form. The rapid what of the technology surprised even its inventors.
items.explanation: After the adjective rapid a noun is required, and adoption is the noun that names the take-up of the technology.
